The publication titled Care Services for Adolescents: A Guide to Implement a Standards-Driven Approach to Improve the Quality of Health-Care Services for Adolescents was released in Geneva in 2015 by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS and the World Health Organization. 2. Ahmed K, Baeten JM, Beksinska M, Bekker LG, Bukusi EA, Donnell D, and colleagues conducted a randomized, multicenter, open-label trial published in The Lancet in 2019. This study examined HIV incidence among women using different contraceptive methods, including intramuscular depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, a copper intrauterine device, or a levonorgestrel implant. 3. 4. Clark JL, Long CM, Giron JM, Cuadros JA, Caceres CF, Coates TJ, and colleagues explored partner notification practices for sexually transmitted diseases in high-risk communities in Peru. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2007. 5. Clark JL, Perez-Brumer A, and Salazar X discussed partner notification, partner management, and conceptual frameworks for HIV/STI control among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Peru. Their work appeared in AIDS and Behavior in 2015. 6. Tan WS and Chio TW conducted a patient preference survey at Singapore's national STI clinic to determine which partner notification methods patients preferred. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2015. 7. A review of national HIV testing policies regarding the age of consent for HIV testing in sub-Saharan Africa was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2019. 8. Quinn C, Wong V, Jamil M, Baggaley R, and Johnson C conducted a scoping review on symptomand risk-based screening tools to optimize provider-initiated HIV testing and counseling in both highand low-HIV-burden settings. This review was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2019. 9. Fox K, Ferguson J, and Ajose W contributed to Annex 15, which reviewed adolescent consent policies for HIV testing in sub-Saharan Africa. This was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2013. 10. The World Health Organization released HIV and Adolescents: Guidance for HIV Testing and Counseling and Care for Adolescents Living with HIV in 2013, providing recommendations for a public health approach and considerations for policymakers and managers. 11. Korenromp EL, Rowley J, Alonso M, Mello MB, Wijesooriya NS, Mahiane SG, and colleagues estimated the global burden of maternal and congenital syphilis and associated adverse birth outcomes for 2016, highlighting progress since 2012. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2019. 12. The Global Hepatitis Report was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2017. 13. The World Health Organization released a Progress Report on HIV, Viral Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infections in Geneva in 2019. 14. The WHO issued an information note in 2017 on the use of dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests. 15. Ishikawa N, Dalal S, Johnson C, Hogan DR, Shimbo T, Shaffer N, and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of universal antenatal HIV testing compared to focused approaches across various HIV prevalence settings. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2016. 16. Meisner J, Rodriguez P, Roberts A, Barnabas R, Newman-Owireddu M, Taylor M, and colleagues modeled the cost-effectiveness of dual maternal HIV and syphilis testing and retesting strategies in highand low-HIV-prevalence countries. This was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2019. 17. The WHO released Consolidated Guidelines on the Use of Antiretroviral Drugs for Treating and Preventing HIV Infection: Recommendations for a Public Health Approach (Second Edition) in 2016. 18. The Guidelines for Managing Advanced HIV Disease and Rapid Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy were published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2017. 19. 20. Kumar AM, Gupta D, Kumar A, Gupta RS, Kanchar A, Rao R, and colleagues conducted operational research in India on implementing routine HIV testing among patients with presumptive tuberculosis. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2016. 21. The WHO released Consolidated Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights of Women Living with HIV in Geneva in 2019. 22. The WHO published Guidelines on Hepatitis B and C Testing in Geneva in 2017. 23. The WHO updated its recommendations on firstand second-line antiretroviral regimens in 2019. 24. Newell M, Coovadia H, Cortina-Borja M, Rollins N, Gaillard P, and Dabis F conducted a pooled analysis on the mortality of infected and uninfected infants born to HIV-infected mothers in Africa. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2004. 25. The WHO released the HIV Molecular Diagnostics Toolkit in 2019 to improve access to viral load testing and infant diagnosis. 26. The WHO published a Public Health Approach to Quality HIV Testing in the Context of Antiretroviral Drugs in 2017. 27. The Country Intelligence Database was released by the WHO in Geneva in 2019. 28. Olaru ID, McHugh G, Dakshina S, Majonga E, Dauya E, Bandason T, and colleagues reported on false-negative HIV tests using oral fluid tests in children on antiretroviral therapy in Harare, Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2017. 29. Were WA, Mermin JH, Wamai N, Awor AC, Bechange S, Moss S, and colleagues studied undiagnosed HIV infection and couple HIV discordance among household members of HIV-infected individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy in Uganda. Their findings were published in JAIDS in 2006. 30. The WHO released the HIV Self-Testing Strategic Framework in 2018, providing guidance for planning, introducing, and scaling up self-testing. 31. Their work was published in JAIDS in 2017. 32. The WHO published Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Testing Services in 2019, emphasizing the need to prioritize undiagnosed individuals and high-risk populations. 33. The WHO released clinical and policy guidelines in 2013 for responding to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women. 34. The WHO, in collaboration with UN Women and UNFPA, published a clinical handbook in 2014 on health care for women subjected to intimate partner violence or sexual violence. 35. The WHO issued clinical guidelines in 2017 for responding to children and adolescents who have been sexually abused. 36. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control published public health guidance in 2018 on screening and vaccination for infectious diseases in newly arrived migrants within the EU/EEA. 37. The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees released guidelines in 2014 for delivering antiretroviral therapy to migrants and crisis-affected individuals in sub-Saharan Africa.
